rationale: C09 is a concrete and material drafting template for the child. Both proclamations implement a new protocol of accession to GATT through nearly the same sequence: recite the original 1947 agreement and implementing proclamations; make the statutory finding concerning burdens on foreign trade; describe notice, consultation, and successful negotiations; identify the new accession protocol and Schedule XX concessions; determine which concessions should initially be applied or withheld; then use a multipart operative scheme applying the protocol subject to its terms, GATT Parts I–III, Schedule XX, the Protocol of Provisional Application, and a more-favorable-treatment exception. The child adapts this machinery from the Annecy Protocol to the Torquay Protocol. C04 and C10 share substantial elements of the same proclamation series but are narrower supplemental or termination instruments and correspond less closely to the child's overall architecture.

shared_material.child_excerpt: on April 21, 1951, I entered, through my duly empowered plenipotentiary, into a trade agreement providing for the accession to the said General Agreement ... which trade agreement consists of the Torquay Protocol to the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade ... including the Annexes thereto
shared_material.parent_excerpt: on October 10, 1949, I entered, through my duly empowered plenipotentiary, into a trade agreement providing for the accession to the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade ... which trade agreement consists of the Annecy Protocol of Terms of Accession ... including the annexes thereto
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive parallel language introduces the later accession protocol by substituting Torquay-specific countries, dates, and instruments into the same drafting frame.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Subject to the provisions of subdivision (b) of this Part, such modifications of existing duties and other import restrictions ... and such continuance of existing customs or excise treatment ... as are specified or provided for in paragraphs 1 to 12 ... of the said Torquay Protocol ... and in Schedule XX contained in Annex A thereto, shall be effective
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Subject to the provisions of subdivision (b) of this part, such modifications of existing duties and other import restrictions ... and such continuance of existing customs or excise treatment ... as are specified or provided for in paragraphs 1 to 13 of the said protocol of accession and in part I of ... schedule XX in annex A thereto shall be effective
shared_material.explanation: The central operative provision is nearly verbatim, with protocol name, paragraph range, and effective date adapted.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The application of the provisions of subdivision (a) ... shall be subject to the applicable terms, conditions, and qualifications set forth in paragraphs 1 to 12 ... in Parts I, II, and III of the said General Agreement ... and in the said Protocol of Provisional Application ... and ... no rate of duty or import tax shall be applied ... if ... more favorable customs treatment is prescribed
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The application of the provisions of subdivision (a) ... shall be subject to the applicable terms, conditions, and qualifications set forth in paragraphs 1 to 13 ... in parts I, II, and III of the said general agreement ... and in said protocol of provisional application ... and ... no rate of duty or import tax shall be applied ... if ... more favorable customs treatment is prescribed
shared_material.explanation: This detailed hierarchy of incorporated instruments and exceptions is the same legal-administrative machinery, not merely generic tariff subject matter.
